title: Test-run evidence never settles a real checkpoint receipt: its record-id check accepts only 64-hex ids, not Engram's 32-hex verification ids
outcome: settle_test_run_verification_receipt (src/test_run_evidence.rs) accepts the verification record ids Engram actually mints (32 lowercase hex digits, as is_engram_record_id accepts; 64 for older ids), so a test run's evidence association records its verification record id and the restart-risk projection clears as designed; a regression uses a 32-hex receipt.
acceptance: settle_test_run_verification_receipt_locked validates the receipt checkpoint id and every verification record id with is_engram_record_id (32 or 64 lowercase hex); the launcher expectedFingerprint keeps its 64-hex SHA-256 validator; every other receipt and association predicate is unchanged.

Deterministic tests cover 32/32, mixed and legacy-64 settlement, settled-id survival across reload and projection, refusal of malformed, duplicate and mismatched receipts, and an unchanged fingerprint rule; they fail at master 4200a0fc and pass on the fix.
Exact-input focused tests, the full five-stage gate and an independent review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
The fix is committed on master and installed.
